# `third_party/pdftex`

Unmodified sources from TeX Live 2026, the source of record for the engine
(`docs/design/engine-v2/DESIGN.md` §4.1: "pdftex.web (TeX Live 2026, pdfTeX
1.40.29, pinned), which already includes e-TeX").

## Pin

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | TeX Live source tree, GitHub mirror <https://github.com/TeX-Live/texlive-source> |
| Tag | `tags/texlive-2026.1` ("texlive-2026.1 tag based on r78399") |
| Commit | `6a300188053b8f2ded89dbd52293732a706b9c0e` |
| Also identical at | `tags/texlive-2026.0`, commit `f26cc5ed05a1f784d1e694fe5b9cfc3ce992c03d` (same `pdftex.web` bytes) |
| Fetched | 2026-09-29 |

## Files

| path | upstream path | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pdftex.web` | `texk/web2c/pdftexdir/pdftex.web` | pdfTeX 3.141592653-2.6-1.40.29; 40,334 lines |
| `etrip/*` except `etrip.tfm` | `texk/web2c/etexdir/etrip/*` | e-TeX's trip test, all 14 files |
| `etrip/etrip.tfm` | derived | `pltotf etrip.pl etrip.tfm` (PLtoTF 3.6, TeX Live 2026) |
| `etrip-oracle/*` | generated | TeX Live 2026's own `pdftex` run on the e-trip test (see below) |

Checksums of every file are in `SHA256SUMS`:

```sh
cd third_party/pdftex && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

`etrip.tfm` is generated so that CI needs no TeX binaries, as
`third_party/knuth/trip/trip.tfm` is. `tftopl etrip.tfm` gives back an
`etrip.pl` byte-identical to the committed one (checked 2026-09-29).
`etrip.pl` is byte-identical to Knuth's `trip.pl`, so `etrip.tfm` equals
`third_party/knuth/trip/trip.tfm`.

## Licence

`pdftex.web` states its own licence:

> pdfTeX is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the
> terms of the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software
> Foundation; either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later
> version.

and, for the e-TeX parts: "Copying of this file is authorized only if (1) you
are P. Breitenlohner, or if (2) you make absolutely no changes to your copy."
It is therefore kept **byte-for-byte unmodified** and is never edited: every
change is a WEB change file in `crates/flashtex-engine/changes/`, applied by
`tools/web2rust` exactly as TANGLE applies one. Because the engine is a
translation of this file, `crates/flashtex-engine` is GPL-2.0-or-later
(`crates/flashtex-engine/LICENSE`); nothing MIT may link it (DESIGN.md §3).
`pdftex.web` may be used only by that crate and this directory.

The e-trip files are e-TeX's (P. Breitenlohner and the NTS team) test suite,
distributed with TeX Live, and are likewise kept unmodified.

## `etrip-oracle/`: what pdfTeX itself does

The e-trip masters in `etrip/` are e-TeX's, from TeX Live 2023's web2c
`etex`. pdfTeX differs from them in a few places for reasons of its own
(its extra primitives, the units `nd` and `nc`, `\vadjust` groups shown as
`\insert0`, its format statistics). The expected output of *this* engine is
therefore pdfTeX's: `etrip-oracle/` holds what TeX Live 2026's `pdftex`
(1.40.29) writes when it runs the e-trip test in the configuration of
`etrip/texmf.cnf`, regenerated by

```sh
scripts/flashtex-etrip.sh --oracle     # needs TeX Live 2026 on PATH
```

MacTeX/TeX Live is an oracle only; it is never in the product path. See
`scripts/flashtex-etrip.sh` for the exact runs and the comparison rules.
